semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {الذين كَفَرُواْ}: the nominative is permissible, as mubtadaʾ (subject), with the sentence from His saying «أضَلَّ أعمالَهم» as the khabar (predicate). The accusative is also permissible by way of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb with a pronoun), by an implied verb that «أضَلَّ» explains in meaning, that is: "He disappointed those who disbelieved."

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {والذين آمَنُواْ}: the two aforementioned options are permissible here. The implied verb is: «رَحِمَ الذين آمنوا» ("He had mercy on those who believed").
His saying: {بِمَا نُزِّلَ على مُحَمَّدٍ}: the majority read it as a passive with shadda. Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Ibn Miqsam read «نَزَّل» as an active verb, the agent being Allah the Exalted. al-Aʿmash read «أُنْزِل» with the hamza of transitivity, passive. «نَزَلَ» was also read as a triliteral active verb.
His saying: «وهو الحقُّ» is a parenthetical clause between the mubtadaʾ and the khabar, or between the explained and the explainer. The explanation of «البال» was given earlier, in Sūrat Ṭāhā.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {ذَلِكَ}: there are two views. The more apparent is that it is a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is the preposition and its noun after it. The second, stated by al-Zamakhsharī, is that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "The matter is that, because of such-and-such"; the preposition and its noun are then in the position of the accusative. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "There is no need for it."
His saying: «كذلك يَضْرِبُ»: al-Zamakhsharī analysed it as: "In the likeness of that striking [of a likeness], Allah strikes their likenesses for the people." The pronoun refers to the two groups, or to the people, in the sense that He strikes their likenesses for the sake of the people so that they may take heed.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {فَإِذَا لَقِيتُمُ}: the operator in this adverbial is an implied verb, the same that operates on «ضَرْبَ الرِّقاب»; its implied form is: "so strike the necks at the time of your meeting the enemy." Abū l-Baqāʾ disallowed that the maṣdar (verbal noun) itself be the operator, saying: "because it is an emphasis." This is one of two views about a maṣdar standing in for its verb, as in «ضَرْباً زيداً»: is the operation attributed to it or to its operator? An example of it:
4050 - على حينَ أَلْهى الناسَ جُلُّ أمورِهمْ ... فنَدْلاً زُرَيْقُ المالَ نَدْلَ الثَّعالبِ
(At a time when most of their affairs had distracted the people, "Snatch, Zurayq, the wealth, as foxes snatch!")
«المالَ» is accusative either by «انْدُلْ» or by «نَدْلاً»; the maṣdar here is annexed to its object. This was used as evidence that the operation belongs to the maṣdar, because it is annexed to what follows it; had it not been an operator it would not have been annexed to what follows.
His saying: «حتى إذا»: this marks the end-point of the command to strike the necks. al-Sulamī read «فَشِدُّوا» with kasra on the shīn, which is very weak. «الوَثاق», with fatḥa (and also with kasra), is the noun for that with which something is tied.
His saying: {فَإِمَّا مَنًّا بَعْدُ وَإِمَّا فِدَآءً}: there are two views about the two words. The better known is that both are accusative as maṣdars of a verb that may not be shown, because whenever a maṣdar is brought to detail the outcome of a sentence, it must be accusative by an implied verb that may not be shown. The implied form is: "either you grant a favour [of release] or you ransom with a ransom." Similar:
4051 - لأَجْهَدَنَّ فإمَّا دَرْءُ واقِعَةٍ ... تُخْشَى وإمَّا بلوغُ السُّؤْلِ والأَمَلِ
(I will surely strive; it will be either the warding off of a feared calamity or the attainment of wish and hope.)
The second view, stated by Abū l-Baqāʾ, is that both are mafʿūl bihi (direct objects) of an implied operator whose implied form is: "grant them a favour, and accept a ransom from them." The Shaykh said: "This is not a grammatical i'rab." Ibn Kathīr read «فِدَى» short. Abū Ḥātim said: "It is not permissible, because it is the maṣdar of «فادَيْتُه»." This is not to be heeded, because al-Farrāʾ reported four dialectal forms of it: the well-known one is with the long vowel; and the i'rab is «فداء لك»; also «فداءٍ» with the long vowel, indeclinable on kasra, with tanwīn, which is very strange. This resembles what some of them say: «هؤلاءٍ» with tanwīn; and «فِدى» with kasra and the short vowel, and «فَدَى» with fatḥa and the short vowel as well.
«الأَوْزارُ» here means the burdens; this is figurative. It is said to be a figure of omission, that is: "the people of war"; and «الأَوْزار» is an expression for the instruments of war. The poet said:
4052 - وأَعْدَدْت للحَرْبِ أوزارَها ... رِماحاً طِوالاً وخَيْلاً ذُكوراً
(I prepared for war its equipment: long spears and male horses.)
The first «حتى» marks the end-point of the striking of the necks, and the second that of «شُدُّوا». It is also permissible that both be end-points of the striking of the necks, with the second being an emphasis (tawkīd) or a badal (substitute).
His saying: «ذلك»: it may be the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "The matter is that"; or it may be accusative by an implied "do".
His saying: «ليَبْلُوَ بَعْضَكم»: that is: "but He commanded you to fight in order to test."
His saying: «قُتِلُوا»: the majority read «قاتلوا»; Abū ʿAmr and Ḥafṣ read «قُتِلوا» as a passive, in the sense that they were killed and died, killing having befallen some of them, as in His saying: {قُتِل مَعَهُ رِبِّيُّونَ}. al-Jaḥdarī read «قَتَلوا» with fatḥa on the qāf and the tāʾ light, its object being omitted. Zayd ibn Thābit, al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā read «قُتِّلوا» with the tāʾ doubled, passive. /
The Commander of the Faithful ʿAlī read «تُضَلَّ» as a passive, «أعمالُهم» in the nominative because it stands in the place of the agent. «تَضِلَّ» was also read with fatḥa on the tāʾ, «أعمالُهم» in the nominative as agent.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {عَرَّفَهَا}: two views are permissible for it. The first: that it is resumptive. The second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), so that "قد" may or may not be taken as implied.
«عَرَّفها» is from «التعريف», which is the opposite of ignorance. It is said to be from «الرَّفْع» (raising). It is said to be from «العَرْف», which is fragrance. Abū ʿAmr, in one transmission, read «ويُدْخِلْهم» with sukūn on the lām, and likewise the mīm of {نُطْعِمُكُمْ} [al-Insān: 9] and the ʿayn of {يَجْمَعُكُمْ} [al-Taghābun: 9], as if he found the vowels heavy. I have read it from him thus in {يُشْعِرُكُمْ} [al-Anʿām: 109] and {يَنصُرُكُمْ} [al-Mulk: 20] and similar words.

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {وَيُثَبِّتْ}: the majority read it with shadda. It is reported from ʿĀṣim that he read it light, from «أَثْبَتَ».

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {والذين كَفَرُواْ}: it may be a mubtadaʾ with its khabar omitted, its implied form being: «فَتَعِسُوا وأُتْعِسُوا» ("so they perished and were made to perish"), as indicated by «فَتَعْساً»; «فتعساً» is accusative by the khabar. The fāʾ has entered by likening the mubtadaʾ to a condition. al-Zamakhsharī supplied the verb that governs «تَعْساً», saying: "because the meaning is: 'He said: perdition' that is, 'He decreed perdition for them.'" The Shaykh said: "To supply a verb of the same wording as the maṣdar is preferable." The second view: that it is accusative by an implied verb that «فتَعْساً لهم» explains, as you say: «زيداً جَدْعاً له» ("Zayd: may he be mutilated"); thus said the Shaykh, following al-Zamakhsharī. But this is not permissible, because «لهم» is not attached to «تَعْساً»; it is attached to something omitted, since it is a clarification, that is: "I mean, for them." The verification of this and the evidence for it have been given before. If the two meant an implied verb merely in terms of general indication, not in terms of ishtighāl, then it is accepted; but their wording rejects that, namely their saying: "accusative by an implied verb that «فَتَعْساً لهم» explains." «أَضَلَّ» is conjoined to that implied verb, that is: "He made them perish and led their deeds astray." «التَّعْسُ» is the opposite of felicity; it is said: «تَعَسَ الرجلُ» with fatḥa, «تَعْساً», and «أَتْعَسَهُ اللَّهُ». Mujammiʿ said:
4053 - تقولُ وقد أَفْرَدْتُها مِنْ حَليلِها ... تَعِسْتَ كما أَتْعَسْتَني يا مُجَمِّعُ
(She says, when I had separated her from her husband: "May you perish, Mujammiʿ, as you have made me perish!")
It is also said «تعِس» with kasra, from Abū l-Haytham, Shamir and others. From Abū ʿUbayda: «تَعَسَه» and «أَتْعَسَه» are both transitive; they are among the verbs in which faʿala and afʿala coincide. It is also said that «التَّعْسُ» is the opposite of recovery (intiʿāsh). al-Zamakhsharī said: "«تَعْساً له» is the opposite of «لَعا له»", meaning that the word «لَعا» means "recover." al-Aʿshā said:
4054 - بذاتِ لَوْثٍ عَفَرْناةٍ، إذا عَثَرَتْ ... فالتَّعْسُ أَدْنى لها مِنْ أَنْ أقولَ لَعَا
(On a strong, sturdy she-camel, when she stumbles, "perdition" is nearer for her than my saying "recover!")
It is also said that «التَّعْسُ» is destruction. It is also said that «التَّعْسُ» is being dragged on the face, and «النَّكْسُ» being dragged on the head.

semin-durr:9-9.t: His saying: {ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ}: «ذلك» may be a mubtadaʾ with the following preposition and its noun as khabar, or the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "The matter is that, because they disliked"; or it may be accusative by an implied verb, that is: "He did that to them because they disliked." In the last two views the preposition and its noun are in the accusative position.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {دَمَّرَ الله عَلَيْهِمْ}: its object may have been omitted, that is: "Allah destroyed their houses and ruined them upon them"; or «دَمَّر» may be given the sense of "Allah was wroth with them, by destroying."
His saying: «أمثالُها»: that is, the like of the preceding outcome. It is said: the likes of the punishment; it is said: of the destruction (al-tadmīra); it is said: of the ruin (al-halaka). The first is preferable because that to which the pronoun returns was mentioned explicitly before, and its meaning is sound.

semin-durr:11-11.t: His saying: {ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّ}: like what he said earlier. «الوَلِيُّ» here means the helper.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {كَمَا تَأْكُلُ الأنعام}: it is either a ḥāl from the pronoun of the maṣdar, that is: "they eat, an eating resembling the eating of cattle"; or an adjective of a maṣdar, that is: "an eating like the eating of cattle."
His saying: {والنار مَثْوًى لَّهُمْ}: this sentence may be resumptive. It may also be a ḥāl, but an anticipated one (muqaddara), that is: "they eat, their abiding in the Fire being anticipated."

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {وَكَأَيِّن مِّن قَرْيَةٍ}: he means the people of a town; hence he took this implied word into account in «أَهْلَكْناهم» and in {فَلاَ نَاصِرَ لَهُمْ}, after having taken the muḍāf into account in His saying «هي أشدُّ». The clause «هي أشدُّ» is an adjective of «قرية». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "He attributed the expulsion to the town, by construing according to the wording, and said «أهلكناهم», construing according to the meaning." The Shaykh said: "The apparent sense of this statement is not sound, because the pronoun in «أهلكناهم» does not refer to the muḍāf of the town to which the expulsion is ascribed, but to the people of the town in His saying {وَكَأَيِّن مِّن قَرْيَةٍ}. [If he meant by 'construing according to the meaning' the meaning of 'town' in {وَكَأَيِّن مِّن قَرْيَةٍ}] then it is sound; but the apparent sense of /his words 'according to the wording' and 'according to the meaning' is that both concern a single referent, and on this «كَأَيِّنْ» would remain loose, with nothing reported of it, unless one imagines that «هي أشدُّ» is a khabar for it; but the apparent view is that it is an adjective of «قرية»." I say: Ibn ʿAṭiyya only meant the wording of «القرية» as a sentence, not as to its specific reference.

semin-durr:14-14.t: His saying: {أَفَمَن كَانَ}: a mubtadaʾ, with the khabar «كَمَنْ زُيِّنَ». It is construed according to the wording of «مَنْ», hence the singular in His saying {لَهُ سواء عَمَلِهِ}, and according to the meaning, hence the plural in His saying {واتبعوا أَهْوَاءَهُمْ}. The clause «اتَّبعوا» is conjoined to «زُيِّنَ», so it is part of the ṣila (relative clause).

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying: {مَّثَلُ الجنة}: there are several views. The first: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is implied. al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl supplied: "The likeness of Paradise is what you hear", so «ما تَسْمعون» is its khabar and «فيها أنهارٌ» explains it. Sībawayh supplied: "In what is recited to you is the likeness of Paradise", and the sentence after it likewise explains the likeness. The second: that «مَثَل» is redundant (zāʾida), the implied form being: "The Paradise promised to the God-fearing has rivers in it." An example of the redundancy of «مَثَل» here is the redundancy of «اسم» in his saying: 4055 - إلى الحَوْلِ ثم اسْمُ السَّلامِ عليكما ... (Until the year, then the name of peace upon you both...)
The third: that «مَثَل الجنة» is the mubtadaʾ and the khabar is His saying «فيها أنهارٌ». This ought to be disallowed, since there is no pronoun returning from the sentence to the mubtadaʾ, and it does not help that the pronoun returns to what the mubtadaʾ is annexed to. The fourth: that «مَثَل الجنة» is the mubtadaʾ and its khabar is {كَمَنْ هُوَ خَالِدٌ فِي النار}. Ibn ʿAṭiyya supplied: "Is the likeness of the people of Paradise like that of one who abides in the Fire?", supplying the particle of denial and a muḍāf so that it be sound. al-Zamakhsharī supplied: "Is the likeness of Paradise like the likeness of the recompense of one who abides in the Fire?" On this view the sentence «فيها أنهارٌ» has three aspects. The first: it is a ḥāl from «الجنة», that is: "established in it are rivers." The second: it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "It has rivers in it", as if a questioner asked, "What is its likeness?" and it was said: "It has rivers in it." The third: that it is a repetition of the ṣila (relative clause), because it is equivalent to it; do you not see that it is sound to say "that which has rivers in it"? The words «مَثَلُ الجنةِ» are bare of the particle of denial in order to depict the obstinacy of one who equates the one who holds fast to the clear proof with the one who follows his desire, like one who equates the Garden whose description is such-and-such with the Fire whose description is that its people are given scalding water to drink. Comparable is the saying of one:
4056 - أَفْرَحُ أَنْ أُرْزَأَ الكرامَ وأَنْ ... أُوْرَثَ ذَوْداً شَصائِصاً نَبْلا
(Shall I rejoice that I am bereaved of noble men and inherit barren, worthless camels?)
It is speech denying joy at being bereaved of the noble and inheriting camels, though bare of the particle of denial. al-Zamakhsharī mentioned all this at greater length than this wording.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib read «مثالَ الجنةِ». From him also, and from Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd: «أمثالُ» in the plural.
His saying: «آسِنٍ»: Ibn Kathīr read «أَسِنٍ» on the pattern of «حَذِرٍ», an active participle of «أَسِنَ» with kasra, «يَأْسَنُ», so it is «أَسِنٌ», like «حَذِرَ يَحْذَر فهو حَذِرٌ». The others read «آسِنٍ» on the pattern of «ضارِب», from «أَسَنَ» with fatḥa, «يَأْسِن». It is said: «أَسَن الماءُ» with fatḥa, «يَأْسِن» and «يَأْسُن» with kasra and ḍamma, «أُسُوْناً»; thus Thaʿlab mentioned it in his «Faṣīḥ». al-Yazīdī said: "It is said «أَسِن» with kasra, «يَأْسَنُ» with fatḥa, «أَسَناً», that is, its taste changed. As for «أسِن الرجلُ», when he enters a well and its smell overcomes him so that dizziness comes upon his head, it is «أَسِن» with kasra only."
The poet said:
4057 - قد أترُكُ القِرْن مُصْفَرَّاً أنامِلُه ... يَميد في الرُّمْح مَيْدَ المائِح الأَسِنِ
(Often I leave the opponent with his fingertips yellowed, swaying on the spear like the dizzy well-diver.)
«يَسِنٍ» was also read, with yāʾ in place of the hamza. Abū ʿAlī said: "It is a lightening of «أَسِنٍ»", and it is a strange lightening.
His saying: {لَّمْ يَتَغَيَّرْ طَعْمُهُ} is an adjective of «لبنٍ». His saying «لذة» may be the feminine of «لَذّ», and «لَذٌّ» means «لذيذ» (delicious), with no figurative interpretation required on this; or it may be a maṣdar used descriptively, with the well-known interpretations. The majority read «لَذَّةٍ» in the genitive as an adjective of «خَمْرٍ»; it was also read in the accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), which supports the maṣdar reading in the majority's recitation; and in the nominative as an adjective of «أنهارٌ». It was not made plural because it is a maṣdar if that is said; and if not, because it is an adjective of a non-rational plural, which is treated as a single feminine.
His saying: «مِنْ عَسَلٍ»: they reported both masculine and feminine for «عَسَل», and the Qurʾān came with the masculine in His saying «مُصَفَّى». «العَسَلان» is running, most used of the wolf; one says «عَسَل الذئبُ والثعلبُ». Its origin is from the «عَسَلان» of a spear, which is its quivering, so the runner as if shakes and moves his limbs. The poet said: /
4058 - لَدْنٌ بِهَزِّ الكفِّ يَعْسِلُ مَتْنُه ... فيه كما عَسَل الطريقَ الثعلبُ
(Supple; when the hand shakes it, its shaft quivers, as the fox runs along the road.)
«بالعُسَيْلة» is used metonymically for sexual intercourse because of what is between them. He, peace be upon him, said: "until you taste his little honey and he tastes your little honey." His saying: {مِن كُلِّ الثمرات}: two views. The first: that this preposition and its noun are an adjective of an implied word, that implied word being a mubtadaʾ and its khabar the preceding prepositional phrase «لهم»; «فيها» is attached to what that is attached to. The implied form is: "and they have in it a pair from every kind of fruit", as if he drew it from His saying: {فِيهِمَا مِن كُلِّ فَاكِهَةٍ زَوْجَانِ} [al-Raḥmān: 52]. Some supplied "a kind (ṣinf)", but the first is more fitting. The second: that «مِنْ» is added to the mubtadaʾ.
His saying: «ومَغْفِرَةٌ»: two views. The first: that it is conjoined to that implied word, without the restriction of being in Paradise, that is: "and they have forgiveness", since forgiveness comes before entering Paradise or just after it. A muḍāf must then be omitted, that is: "and the bliss of forgiveness", because it arises from forgiveness, and it is in Paradise.
The second: that its khabar is made implied, that is: "and for them is forgiveness", and the sentence is resumptive. The difference between the two views is that in the preceding view the predication is by the pronounced «لهم» about the course of that omitted word and «مغفرة», while in the other view the khabar is another preposition and noun, omitted because it is indicated.
His saying: «كمَنْ هو»: it has been said earlier that it may be the khabar of «مَثَلُ الجنة» by the two interpretations mentioned from Ibn ʿAṭiyya and al-Zamakhsharī. But if we do not make it a khabar of «مَثَل», there are four views. The first: that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "Is the state of these God-fearing like the state of one who abides...?" This is a sound interpretation. Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned the remaining views and said: "It is in the position of the nominative, that is: their state is like the state of one who abides in the Fire.
It is also said: it is mockery of them. It is also said: it has the meaning of a question, that is: 'Is it like one who abides...?' It is also said: it is in the position of the accusative, that is: they resemble the state of one who abides in the Fire." End. The meaning of his saying "It is also said: it is mockery" is that the statement 'their state is like the state of one who...' is made by way of mockery and sarcasm.
His saying: «وسُقُوا» is conjoined to the ṣila, a verbal sentence conjoined to a nominal one; but he took the wording of «مَنْ» into account in the first and so used the singular, and its meaning in the second and so used the plural.
«الأَمْعاءُ» is the plural of «مِعىً» with the short vowel, which is the intestine in the belly; it has been described in the plural, as in the verse:
4059 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ومِعَىً جياعا
(... and hungry intestines.)
meaning the genus. Its alif is from yāʾ, as shown by their saying «مِعَيان» (dual).

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {آنِفاً}: two views. The first: that it is accusative as a ḥāl; Abū l-Baqāʾ supplied: "What did he say, beginning it (muʾtanifan)?" Others supplied: "commencing", that is: "What is the speech he has just begun, before leaving it?" The second: that it is accusative as an adverbial, that is: "What did he say just now (al-sāʿa)?", said by al-Zamakhsharī. The Shaykh denied this, saying: "Because we do not know anyone who counted it among the adverbials." Their wordings differ about its meaning: the apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's wording is that it is a temporal adverbial like «الآن», hence he explained it as «الساعة». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The exegetes say that «آنِفاً» means the past moment close to us, and this is an explanation by meaning."
al-Bazzī, with a difference reported from him, read «أَنِفاً» with the short vowel. The others read it with the long vowel; both are dialects with one meaning, and both are active participles, like «حاذِر» and «حَذِر», «آسِن» and «أَسِن», except that no plain verb is used for them; what is used is «ائْتَنَفَ يَأْتَنِفُ» and «اسْتَأْنف يَسْتأنف». «الائْتِنافُ» and «الاسْتِئْناف» mean beginning. al-Zajjāj said: "It is from «اسْتَأْنَفْتُ الشيءَ» when you begin it, that is: 'What did he say in the first moment close to us?'"

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {والذين اهتدوا}: the nominative is permissible as a mubtadaʾ, and the accusative by ishtighāl. «تَقْواهم» is a maṣdar annexed to its agent. The pronoun in «آتاهم» refers to Allah, or to the saying of the hypocrites, since that saying of theirs increases the believers in God-fearing, or to the Messenger.

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying: {أَن تَأْتِيَهُمْ}: a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from «الساعة». Abū Jaʿfar al-Ruʾāsī read «إنْ تَأْتِهم» with the conditional «إنْ» and the jussive after it. There are two views about its apodosis. The first: that it is His saying «فأنَّى لهم», said by al-Zamakhsharī. Then he said: "If you say: to what is His saying {فَقَدْ جَآءَ أَشْرَاطُهَا} connected on the two readings? I say: to the coming of the Hour, as the connection of the cause with the effect, as you say: 'If Zayd honours me, then I am worthy of honour; I honour him.'" The second: that the apodosis is His saying {فَقَدْ جَآءَ أَشْرَاطُهَا}, and though the coming of the Hour is certain, they were treated as one in doubt, and such was their state.
«الأَشْراط» is the plural of «شَرْط», with sukūn on the rāʾ / or with fatḥa. Abū l-Aswad said:
4060 - فإن كنتِ قد أَزْمَعْتِ بالصَّرْمِ بَيْنَنَا ... فقد جَعَلَتْ أَشْراطُ أَوَّلِه تَبْدو
(If you have resolved on a break between us, the signs of its beginning have started to show.)
«الأشراط» are the signs; from it come the «أَشْراط الساعة» (portents of the Hour). «أَشْرَطَ الرجلُ نفسَه» means he bound himself to certain matters. Aws said:
4061 - فأَشْرَطَ فيها نَفْسَه وهو مُعْصِمٌ ... فأَلْقَى بأسبابٍ له وتَوَكَّلا
(He committed himself to it while holding fast, and cast his ropes and put his trust in God.)
«الشَّرْطُ» is also cutting, the maṣdar of «شَرَطَ الجلدَ يَشْرِطُه (يَشْرُطُه) شَرْطاً».
His saying: «فَأَنَّى لهم»: «أنَّى» is a fronted khabar and «ذِكْراهم» a postponed mubtadaʾ, that is: "How can they have the reminder?" «إذا» and what follows it is parenthetical and its apodosis is omitted, that is: "How can they have the reminder when the Hour comes to them? How will they then take heed?" It is also possible that the mubtadaʾ is omitted, that is: "How can they have deliverance", and «ذِكْراهم» is the agent of «جاءَتْهم».
Abū ʿAmr, in one transmission, read «بَغَتَّةً» with fatḥa on the ghayn and doubled tāʾ; it is an adjective, so its accusative is as ḥāl; it has no parallel among adjectives or maṣdars; such forms occur only among nouns, like «الجَرَبَّة» for a group and «الشَّرَبَّة» for a place. al-Zamakhsharī said: "I fear that this is a slip by the transmitter from Abū ʿAmr, and that the correct form is «بَغَتَةً» with fatḥa and no doubling."

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying: {لَوْلاَ نُزِّلَتْ}: this has the meaning of «هَلاَّ» ("why not"). No heed is to be paid to the saying of some that «لا» is redundant and the original is «لو نُزِّلَتْ». The majority read «سورةٌ مُحْكَمَةٌ» in the nominative as it stands in the place of the agent. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read both in the accusative as ḥāl, the deputy agent being a pronoun for the earlier sūra; the occurrence of a ḥāl is justified by the description, as you say «الرجل جاءني رجلاً صالحاً». It was also read: {فَإِذَآ نَزَلَتْ سُورَةٌ}. Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Ibn ʿUmayr read «وذَكَرَ» as active, that is, Allah the Exalted, with «القتالَ» in the accusative.
His saying: «نَظَرَ المَغْشِيِّ»: the original is «نَظَراً مِثْلَ نَظَر المَغْشِيِّ».
His saying: {فأولى لَهُمْ طَاعَةٌ}: the lexicographers and the grammarians differed about this word. al-Aṣmaʿī said: it is a past verb meaning "he came close to what destroys him", and he cited:
4062 - فعادَى بينَ هادِيَتَيْنِ مِنْها ... وَأَوْلَى أَنْ يزيدَ على الثلاثِ
(He drove between two leading ones of them, and came close to exceeding three.)
that is: he came close to exceeding. Thaʿlab said: "No one has said anything better about «أَوْلَى» than al-Aṣmaʿī's statement." But most say it is a noun. These then differed: it is said that it is derived from «الوَلْي», which is nearness, as in:
4063 - يُكَلِّفُني لَيْلَى وقد شَطَّ وَلْيُها ... وعادَتْ عَوادٍ بيننا وخُطُوْبُ
(He burdens me with Laylā, though her nearness is far off, and obstacles and calamities have returned between us.)
It is also said that it is derived from «الوَيْل». The original is «أَوْيَل», the ʿayn was transposed to after the lām, so its pattern became «أَفْلَع». Al-Jurjānī leaned to this. The principle is that there is no transposition. As for its meaning: it is said to be a threat and warning, as in:
4064 - فأَوْلَى ثم أَوْلَى ثم أَوْلَى ... وهَلْ للدَرِّ يُحْلَبُ مِنْ مَرَدِّ
(Woe, then woe, then woe! And is there any returning for milk once it has been milked?)
al-Mubarrad said: it is said to one who is about to become angry «أَوْلَى لك», like the saying of a Bedouin who kept shooting game that escaped him, and would say «أَوْلى لك»; then he shot some game and nearly caught it, but it escaped him, so he said:
4065 - فلو كان أَوْلَى يُطْعِمُ القومَ صِدْتُهم ... ولكنَّ أَوْلى يَتْرُكُ القومَ جُوَّعا
(If "awlā" could feed the people, I would have hunted for them; but "awlā" leaves the people hungry.)
That is what concerns its derivation and meaning. As for the i'rab: if we follow the majority's view, there are several views. The first: «أَوْلَى» is a mubtadaʾ and «لهم» its khabar, the implied form being: "So destruction is theirs." The beginning with an indefinite is justified by its being a supplication, like {ويْلٌ لِّكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ} [al-Humaza: 1]. The second: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, the implied form being: punishment or destruction is nearer to them, that is, closer and nearer. The lām may also mean the bāʾ, that is: "more fitting and more deserving of them". The third: that it is a mubtadaʾ with «لهم» attached to it, the lām meaning bāʾ, and «طاعةٌ» is its khabar, the implied form being: "Obedience, rather than anything else, is more fitting for them." If we follow al-Aṣmaʿī's view, it is a past verb with a latent agent which the context indicates, as if it were said: "so it (that is, destruction) drew near", and this is the apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's wording when he said: "Its meaning is a supplication against them, that the disliked thing befall them." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: / "The well-known Arab usage is that you say: 'This is more fitting for you than this' (awlā bika), that is, more deserving. The Arabs also use «أَوْلَى» alone, by way of omission and brevity because of the words that go with it, saying «أَوْلَى لك يا فلانُ» by way of rebuke and threat." End.
Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«أَوْلَى» is a feminine; its plural is «أَوْلات»." There is room for doubt in this, because that applies only to true masculine and feminine, whereas for the verbal (formal) feminine it is not said. More explanation will come in Sūrat al-Qiyāma, God willing.
His saying: {طَاعَةٌ}: several views. The first: that it is the khabar of «أَوْلَى لهم» as above. The second: that it is an adjective of «سورةٌ», that is: "when a firmly-worded sūra is sent down, obedient", that is, possessed of obedience or obeyed. Makkī and Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned it, and it is remote because of the many intervening elements. The third: that it is a mubtadaʾ and «قولٌ» is conjoined to it, with an omitted khabar, the implied form being: "is more fitting for you than anything else." Makkī supplied: "From us is obedience", supplying it fronted. The fourth: that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is: "Our command is obedience." The fifth: that «لهم» is a fronted khabar and «طاعةٌ» a postponed mubtadaʾ; the pausing and beginning are known from what I presented earlier, so consider it.
His saying: «فإذا عَزَمَ»: there are three views about its apodosis. The first: His saying «فلو صَدَقُوا», as in «إذا جاءني طعامٌ فلو جِئْتَني أطعمتُك» ("If food comes to me, were you to come to me I would feed you"). The second: that it is omitted, its implied form being "so be truthful"; thus Abū l-Baqāʾ supplied it. The third: that its implied form is "so carry out". It is also said: its implied form is "they disliked that". «عَزَمَ الأمرُ» is by figurative predication, as in his saying: 4066 - قد جَدَّتِ الحربُ بكم فَجُدُّوا ... (War has become serious with you, so be serious...)
or it is on the omission of a muḍāf, that is: "the people of the matter resolved."

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {أَن تُفْسِدُواْ}: the khabar of «عسى». The condition is parenthetical between them, and its apodosis is omitted because «فهل عَسَيْتُم» indicates it, or «فهل عَسَيْتُمْ» explains it according to those who allow it to be fronted. ʿAlī read «إنْ تُوُلِّيْتُمْ» with ḍamma on the tāʾ and the wāw and kasra on the lām, passive, from «الوِلاية» (authority), that is: "if you are given authority over the affairs of the people." «وُلِّيْتُمْ» was also read, likewise from authority. These two readings indicate that «تَوَلَّيْتُمْ» in the majority reading is from that same root; it may also be from turning away, which is the apparent sense. In His saying «عَسَيْتُمْ» to the end there is an iltifāt (shift of person) from the third person in His saying {الذين فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَّرَضٌ} to addressing them with that, to increase their rebuke.
The majority read «وتُقَطِّعوا» with doubling, for intensification. Abū ʿAmr in one transmission, Sallām and Yaʿqūb read it light, the imperfect of «قَطَعَ». al-Ḥasan read it with fatḥa on the tāʾ and the ṭāʾ doubled; its original is «تَتَقَطَّعوا» with two tāʾs, one of which was dropped. On this «أرحامَكم» is accusative by removal of the preposition, that is: "in your wombs (kinship ties)."

semin-durr:23-23.t: His saying: {أولئك}: a mubtadaʾ, and the relative noun is its khabar. The implied form is: "Those corrupters", as indicated by what came before. And His saying «فأَصَمَّهم»; He did not say "so He deafened their ears", and «أَعْمى أَبْصَارهم»; He did not say "He blinded them". It is said: because the loss of the ear does not necessarily entail the loss of hearing, so He did not mention it, whereas the eyes, which are the «أَبْصار», their loss necessarily entails the loss of sight. {في آذَانِهِمْ وَقْرٌ} [Fuṣṣilat: 44] and the like is no objection to you, because it is less than deafness, and deafness is greater than it.

semin-durr:24-24.t: His saying: {أَمْ على قُلُوبٍ}: «أم» is munqaṭiʿa (disjunctive); you know what is said about it. The majority read «أَقْفالُها» in the plural on the pattern «أَفْعال». «أَقْفُلُها» on the pattern «أَفْعُل» was also read. «إقْفالُها» with kasra on the hamza was also read, as a maṣdar like «الإِقبال». This statement is an eloquent metaphor, made to express the failure of the truth to reach them.

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {الشيطان سَوَّلَ}: this sentence is the khabar of {إِنَّ الذين ارتدوا}. The discussion of «سَوَّل» as to meaning and derivation has already been given. al-Zamakhsharī said here: "Someone with no knowledge of either morphology or derivation derived it from «السُّؤْل»", as if he alluded to what Ibn Baḥr said: that the meaning is "he gave them what they asked for (suʾlahum)". The error in it is that the root of «السُّؤْل» is from «السؤال» with a hamza, while the root of this one is with a wāw; so they differ. Had it been as said, it would have been said «سَأَّل» with a doubled hamza, not with a wāw. There is room for doubt in what al-Zamakhsharī said, because «السؤال» has two roots: «سَأَل» with hamza, and «سال» with an alif converted from wāw, on which is the reading «سال سايل» and his saying:
4067 - سالَتْ هُذَيْلٌ رسولَ الله فاحِشةً ... ضَلَّتْ هُذَيْلٌ بما سالَتْ ولم تُصِبِ
(Hudhayl asked the Messenger of Allah for a shameful thing; Hudhayl went astray in what it asked and did not hit the mark.)
This has been covered in full in al-Baqara.
His saying: «وأَمْلَى»: the majority read «أَمْلَى» active, the agent being the pronoun of Satan. It is also said that it refers to the Creator, the Exalted. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "On the first it is conjoined to the khabar, on the second it is resumptive." What he said is not necessary; rather it is conjoined to the khabar on both views: He reports of them this and that. Abū ʿAmr, among others, read «أُمْلِيَ» passive, the deputy agent being the preposition and its noun. It is also said that the deputy agent is the pronoun of Satan, mentioned by Abū l-Baqāʾ, but there is no sense in that. Yaʿqūb, Sallām and Mujāhid / read «وأُمْلِيْ» with ḍamma on the hamza, kasra on the lām and sukūn on the yāʾ. This allows two views. The first: that it is an imperfect predicated of the first-person pronoun, that is: "and I give them respite"; the second: that it is a past verb as in Abū ʿAmr's reading, with its yāʾ made quiescent for lightness. A good deal of this has already passed.

semin-durr:26-26.t: His saying: {إِسْرَارَهُمْ}: the two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Ḥafṣ read it with kasra on the hamza, as a maṣdar; the others read it with fatḥa, as the plural of «سِرّ».

semin-durr:27-27.t:
His saying: {فَكَيْفَ}: it is either a fronted khabar, that is: "How then will His knowledge of their secrets be when the angels take them?"; or accusative by an omitted verb, that is: "How will they act?"; or the khabar of an implied «كان», that is: "How will they be?" The adverbial is governed by that implied element.
al-Aʿmash read «تَوَفَّاهم» without tāʾ, which allows two views: that it is a past verb as in the majority reading, or an imperfect with one of its two tāʾs dropped.
His saying: «يَضْرِبُون»: a ḥāl, either from the agent, which is the more apparent, or from the object.

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying: {أَن لَّن يُخْرِجَ}: this «أنْ» is the lightened one; «لن» and what follows it is its khabar, and its ism (noun) is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). «الأَضْغان» is the plural of «ضِغْن», which means rancours; «الضَّغِينة» is the same. He said:
4068 - وذي ضِغْنٍ كَفَفْتُ الوُدَّ عنه ... وكنتُ على إساءَتِه مُقِيتا
(Of one full of rancour I withheld my affection, yet I remained a provider for him despite his wrongdoing.)
And ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm said:
4069 - فإنَّ الضِّغْنَ بعد الضِّغْنِ يَغْشُو ... عليكَ ويُخْرِجُ الداء الدَّفينا
(For rancour after rancour comes upon you and brings out the buried disease.)
It is also said: «الضِّغْنُ» is enmity. And it was recited:
4070 - قُلْ لابنِ هندٍ ما أردْتَ بمنطقٍ ... ساء الصديقَ وشَيَّد الأضغانا
(Say to Ibn Hind: what did you intend by speech that hurt the friend and built up rancours?)
One says «ضَغِنَ» with kasra, «يَضْغَنُ» with fatḥa, and «ضُغِنَ عليه»; «اضْطَغَنَ القومُ» and «تَضاغنوا». The root originally is from crookedness in the legs of an animal and in a spear shaft. He said: 4071 - إنَّ قناتي مِنْ صَليباتِ القَنا ... ما زادَها التثقيفُ إلاَّ ضَغَنا
(My lance is of the hardest lances; straightening only increased its crookedness.)
Another said:
4072 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كذاتِ الضِّغْنِ تَمْشي في الرِّفاقِ
(... like the one with a grudge walking among the companions.)
«الاضْطِّغانُ» is also embracing something. From it is their saying «اضْطَغَنْتُ الصبيَّ», that is, I took the child to myself; and he recited:
4073 - كأنه مُضْطَغِنٌ صَبِيَّا ...
(As if he were holding a child to himself...)
And another said:
4074 - وما اضْطَغَنْتُ سِلاحي عند مَغْرِضِها ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I did not clasp my weapon at its target...)
«فرسٌ ضاغِنٌ» is a horse that runs only when struck.

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying: {لأَرَيْنَاكَهُمْ}: from seeing with the eye. It came in the most eloquent form, with the two pronouns attached; had it come as «أَرَيْناك إياهم» it would have been permissible.
His saying: «فَلَعَرَفْتَهُمْ» is conjoined to the apodosis of «لو». His saying «ولَتَعْرِفَنَّهم» is the answer to an omitted oath.
His saying: {فِي لَحْنِ القول}: «اللحن» is said in two senses. The first: allusion in speech so that no one but the one you address understands it. From it is the saying of al-Qattāl al-Kilābī in a story of his:
4075 - ولقد وَحَيْتُ لكم لكيما تَفْهموا ... ولَحَنْتُ لَحْناً ليس بالمُرْتابِ
(I signalled to you so that you might understand, and I spoke an allusion that leaves no doubt.)
Another said:
4076 - منطِقٌ صائبٌ وتَلْحَنُ أَحْيا ... ناً وخيرُ الحديثِ ما كان لَحْناً
(Speech that is correct, and at times you speak allusively; the best talk is that which is allusive.)
«اللَّحْنُ» is also turning speech from correct i'rab to error. It is said that what unites it with the first is turning speech away from its proper course. From the first one says «لَحَنْتُ» with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ, «أَلْحَنُ له», so I am «لاحِنٌ»; and «ألحنتُه الكلامَ» means I made him understand it, so he «لَحِنَه» with kasra, that is, understood it, and is «لاحِنٌ». From the second one says «لَحِن» with kasra when he does not use i'rab, so he is «لَحِنٌ».

semin-durr:31-31.t: His saying: {وَلَنَبْلُوَنَّكُمْ حتى}: Abū Bakr read «ولَيَبْلوَنَّكم حتى يَعْلم ويبلوَ أخبارَكم», all three with yāʾ (from below), meaning Allah the Exalted. al-Aʿmash likewise, with sukūn on the wāw; the others read with the nūn of majesty, and Ruways likewise, with sukūn on the wāw. The apparent sense, in the reading with sukūn on the wāw, is that it is cut off from the first. It is possible that he made the wāw quiescent for lightness, like al-Ḥasan's reading {أَوْ يَعْفُوْ الذي} with sukūn on the wāw.

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying: {وتدعوا إِلَى السلم}: the jussive is permissible, conjoined to the prohibitive verb; and the accusative by an implied «أَنْ» in the answer to a prohibition. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read it with the dāl doubled. al-Zamakhsharī said: "From «ادَّعَى القومُ» and «تداعَوْا», like «ارتَمَوْا إلى الصيد» and «تَرَامَوْا»." Others said it means "you boast", meaning "you claim lineage". The disagreement about «السّلم» has been given earlier.
His saying: «وأنتم الأَعْلَوْن»: a ḥāl clause. Likewise «والله معكم». The original of «الأَعْلَوْنَ» is «الأَعْلَيُون», which underwent weakening changes.
His saying: «يَتِرَكُمْ»: that is, He will diminish you, or isolate you from them (your deeds); it is from «وَتَرْتُ الرجلَ» when you killed one of his people or plundered his property; or from «الوِتْر», which is being alone. It is also said that both meanings go back to isolation, since one whose slain one was killed or whose property was plundered / has been isolated from it.

semin-durr:37-37.t:
His saying: {فَيُحْفِكُمْ}: conjoined to the condition, and «تَبْخَلوا» is the apodosis.
His saying: «ويُخْرِجْ أَضْغانَكم»: the majority attribute the verb to a pronoun-agent: either Allah the Exalted, or the Messenger, or the asking, because it is a cause; and it is jussive by conjunction to the apodosis. From Abū ʿAmr it is reported in the nominative as resumptive. He also read it with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the rāʾ, with «أَضْغانُكم» nominative as agent of its verb. Ibn ʿAbbās, among others, read «وتَخْرُجْ» with tāʾ (from above) and ḍamma on the rāʾ, «أضغانُكم» being its agent. Yaʿqūb read «ونُخْرِجْ» with the nūn of majesty and kasra on the rāʾ, «أضغانَكم» accusative.
«يُخْرَجْ» was also read with yāʾ, passive, «أَضْغانُكم» nominative by it. ʿĪsā likewise, except that he put it in the accusative by an implied «أَنْ», conjoined to a supposed maṣdar, that is: "Your miserliness and the bringing out of your rancours will occur."

semin-durr:38-38.t:
His saying: {هَا أَنتُمْ هؤلاء}: al-Zamakhsharī said: «هؤلاء» is a relative noun whose ṣila is «تَدْعُوْن», that is: "You are those who are called", or "you, O addressed ones, are these described ones"; then he began a resumptive description of them, as though they said: "And what is our description?" and it was said: "You are called." I say: this has been discussed at length in Sūrat Āl ʿImrān.
His saying: {يَبْخَلُ عَن نَّفْسِهِ}: «بَخِلَ» and «ضَنَّ» are transitive sometimes with «على» and sometimes with «عن». The better course is that, when they are made transitive with «عن», they are taken to include the sense of withholding.
His saying: «وإنْ تَتَوَلَّوْا»: this conditional sentence is conjoined to the conditional before it, and {ثُمَّ لاَ يكونوا} is conjoined to «يَسْتَبْدِلْ».
